podcast.title: "General Utility Singer" at Motown
podcast.body: Anne Bogan was a versatile vocalist known as a "general utility singer" around Motown. She sang with The Andantes and The Changes 3, performed duets with Harvey Fuqua, and even toured as a substitute for Tammi Terrell with Marvin Gaye. "Anne was a sort of general utility singer around Motown. She'd sung with the Andantes and the Changes 3"

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
srcs.episode: Episode 93: "Please Mr. Postman" by the Marvelettes

podcast.title: Replacement for Gladys Horton
podcast.body: Harvey Fuqua suggested Anne Bogan to replace Gladys Horton in The Marvelettes after Gladys's departure. Anne joined the group for their final two albums and was given opportunities to sing on album tracks. "Harvey Fouque was suggested Anne Bogan, who he'd discovered a while before, and recorded a few duets with. Anne was a sort of general utility singer around Motown. She'd sung with the Andantes and the Changes 3, and she'd also gone out on the road with Marvin Gaye, sobbing for his duet partner, Tamri Terrell, when the latter had become sick with the brain tumor that eventually killed her. Anne replaced Gladys, and the group made two further albums, and Anne was at least allowed to sing on album tracks."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs
